name: Coinbase (Beta)
description: Beta Coinbase trading engine for Crow. Practice mode is the default: orders are simulated against public market data, and live trading is switched on separately, in the Trading panel. Every order from a bot or the AI goes through one gateway with caps.
author: Crow

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_PROJECT_ID
env_vars.description: The Crow project that owns the trading audit trail. Set by the Trading panel when you connect.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_ENGINE_URL
env_vars.description: Where Crow's MCP server reaches the trading engine on this computer. Leave it as it is.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_ENGINE_TOKEN
env_vars.description: Bearer token Crow's MCP server and panel use to reach the engine's API on loopback. Generated by Crow at install; never shown.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_LIVE
env_vars.description: Safety ceiling. Set to false to forbid live trading on this computer no matter what the Trading page says.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_POLL_SECONDS
env_vars.description: Seconds between engine ticks (market read, fill check, reconcile).

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_MAKER_FEE_PCT
env_vars.description: Maker fee percent per fill. A grid step must clear twice this fee plus a margin.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_PRODUCTS
env_vars.description: Comma-separated Coinbase products the engine may trade, on its practice book and on its live book alike.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_DAILY_NOTIONAL_USD
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the total USD value of orders the engine may place per UTC day, across all products and owners. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_ORDERS_PER_HOUR
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the number of orders the engine may place in any rolling hour, across all products and owners. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_PORTFOLIO_DRAWDOWN_PCT
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the portfolio drawdown percent from its high-water mark at which the engine halts new orders on that book until the halt is cleared. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_BOT_MAX_ORDER_USD
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the largest single order, in USD, a bot may place. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_MAX_BOT_CAPITAL_USD
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the largest starting capital, in USD, a new bot may be created with. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_AI_MAX_ORDER_USD
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the value, in USD, of a single order the AI may place. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_AI_DAILY_NOTIONAL_USD
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the total USD value of orders the AI may place per UTC day. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_AI_ORDERS_PER_HOUR
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the number of orders the AI may place in any rolling hour. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_AI_CAPITAL_USD
env_vars.description: Ceiling for the capital, in USD, the AI may manage. Settings in the Trading panel can lower it but never raise it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_AI_ORDER_MODE
env_vars.description: How the AI's orders go out. `approve` means the AI previews each order and you approve it in the Crow dashboard; `autonomous` is not available yet.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_AI_PREVIEW_TTL_S
env_vars.description: Seconds a previewed AI order stays open for your approval before it expires.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_TRAIL_ALERT_DAYS
env_vars.description: Days a bot may do worse than simply holding its starting mix before the engine raises an alert and suggests pausing it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_PRODUCTS
env_vars.description: Stocks are off while this is empty. Set a comma-separated list of stock ids, such as NVDA-USD, to let Crow trade them. Each one is a stock Coinbase trades, and a stock may not share its underlying asset with a crypto product.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_LIVE
env_vars.description: Live stock trading cannot be turned on yet. It needs a confirmed order preview, which comes in a later step; until then stock orders stay in practice.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_MAX_ORDER_USD
env_vars.description: The most, in USD, for one stock order the AI may place. Set it here; the Trading panel cannot change it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_DAILY_NOTIONAL_USD
env_vars.description: The most total USD value of stock orders the AI may place per UTC day. Set it here; the Trading panel cannot change it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_AI_CAPITAL_USD
env_vars.description: The money, in USD, set aside for the AI's stock trades. Zero means the AI may not buy a stock. Set it here; the Trading panel cannot change it.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_DRAWDOWN_ALERT_PCT
env_vars.description: How far your stock holdings may fall from their high point, in percent, before Crow raises an alert. It alerts only; trading carries on.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_EQUITY_PORTFOLIO_ID
env_vars.description: Reserved for a later step. Leave it empty.

env_vars.name: CROW_COINBASE_WATCHDOG_POLICY
env_vars.description: What the watchdog does when the engine's heartbeat goes stale: `leave` raises an alert only; `cancel` also cancels the engine's own open orders (those whose client order id starts with cb-).

notes: This is a beta. Practice mode is the default: orders are limit and post-only, and fills are simulated against public market data. Live trading stays off until it is switched on in the Trading panel, and the CROW_COINBASE_LIVE ceiling can forbid it on a machine entirely. A halt stops new orders: the kill switch stops both books and cancels the engine's resting cb- orders, while a book's own portfolio drawdown stop stops that book alone and cancels that book's resting orders too, leaving the other book untouched. Clearing a halt needs an explicit acknowledgement that re-bases each book's high-water mark.
